decisions.reason: As a core upholstery fabric that is very close to the firm's established capabilities and has remained prominently presented, it is more likely to be refined through the firm's existing design and R&D knowledge than withdrawn.

This decorative fabric still fits the firm's knowledge base well, but its weaker website prominence and broader portfolio-pruning logic leave it with a somewhat higher risk than the lead products despite likely ongoing learning from market feedback.

The flame-retardant jacquard curtain fabric aligns strongly with the firm's functional and contract-textile expertise, so absorptive capacity and continued demand for performance interiors make retention the most likely outcome.

Although newer and therefore less proven, this braided-structure upholstery and curtain fabric builds directly on the firm's existing textile know-how and was given strong visibility, which supports further development rather than exit.
